title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Studying, Publicizing and Implementing the Revised Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Conscientiously Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Revised Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [1997] No. 3

To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

The revised Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China has been adopted by the Fifth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress and shall come into force on October 1, 1997. The Criminal Law is the basic law of the State and an important legal basis for the People's Courts in trying criminal cases. The revision of the Criminal Law is a major event in improving the socialist legal system and an important step in perfecting China's criminal legislation and judicial system, attracting widespread attention both domestically and internationally. Conscientiously studying, publicizing, and implementing the revised Criminal Law is of great significance for the People's Courts to further enhance their level of law enforcement and better fulfill their duty to combat crime and protect the people. For the correct implementation of the revised Criminal Law, the following notice is hereby issued:

1. People's Courts at all levels shall conscientiously organize adjudicators to study the revised Criminal Law. The revised Criminal Law carefully summarizes the practical experience of implementing the Criminal Law over the past 17 years, draws on legislative experience from domestic and foreign criminal laws, clearly stipulates the basic principles of the Criminal Law; highlights the protection of the socialist market economic order; adapts to the practical needs of combating criminal activities by providing clearer and more detailed provisions on some common and frequently occurring crimes that have drawn strong public reaction; stipulates corresponding criminal liability for newly emerging criminal acts that require investigation; and revises and improves some important criminal law systems. It is a more scientific, unified, and complete criminal code. People's Courts at all levels shall formulate study plans, adopt various forms, and continuously deepen their study to truly understand and master it.

2. People's Courts at all levels shall, in light of local actual conditions and in coordination with relevant departments, extensively and deeply carry out publicity activities for the revised Criminal Law. The revised Criminal Law is a powerful weapon for judicial organs to strike at and punish crime and will have a significant impact on many aspects of social, political, and economic life. People's Courts shall give full play to the advantages of adjudicative work, through news media and other forms, with an emphasis on key points, to carry out targeted publicity of the revised Criminal Law.

3. After the revised Criminal Law comes into effect, People's Courts at all levels must resolutely implement it. For acts committed before the revised Criminal Law comes into effect, which have not yet been handled or are being handled after October 1, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 12 of the revised Criminal Law; for cases that had been finally adjudicated by the People's Courts before the revised Criminal Law came into effect and are retried by the People's Courts under the adjudicative supervision procedure after the law comes into effect, the relevant legal provisions in force at the time of the original final adjudication shall apply.

4. Before the revised Criminal Law comes into effect, the People's Courts in adjudicating criminal cases shall still apply the current Criminal Law and the relevant decisions and supplementary provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress amending or supplementing the Criminal Law, as well as the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, and shall comply with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law concerning procedures and time limits.

5. After the revised Criminal Law comes into effect, the relevant decisions and supplementary provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress that have been expressly repealed, and the original judicial interpretations made by the Supreme People's Court, shall no longer apply. However, if the substantive content of the relevant provisions of the revised Criminal Law has not changed, the People's Courts may, in criminal adjudicative work, apply them by reference in the absence of new judicial interpretations. Other judicial interpretations that conflict with the provisions of the revised Criminal Law shall no longer apply.

6. In the course of studying, publicizing, and implementing the revised Criminal Law, People's Courts at all levels shall strengthen investigation and research, pay attention to collecting major and difficult issues encountered in understanding and applying the law, and promptly report them to higher authorities.

It is hereby notified.

March 25, 1997
